children: steady start Stock closes Nearly 2% Higher Our Bureau Mumbai: Shares of the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) made their stock market debut at 1,800 apiece on the BSE on Thursday, a 0.84% premium over the issue price of 1,785, marking the culmination of a nearly decade-long wait for the country's largest bourse to enter the public markets.

The stock closed at 1,818, up nearly 2% from the issue price, after touching a high of 1,878 earlier in the day. At Thursday's closing price, the NSE was valued at about 4.49 lakh crore, compared with the listed rival BSE's market capitalisation of around 1.33 lakh crore. The NSE ranked 11th among India's listed companies by market capitalisation.

Reliance Industries remained the country's most valuable company, followed by HDFC Bank and Bharti Airtel. NSE shares were listed on the BSE and Metropolitan Stock Exchange (MSE). About 51.5 million shares changed hands on the BSE and 177,000 shares on the MSE on Thursday.

The 22,569-crore initial public offering (IPO) was subscribed 5.71 times by the close of bidding on September 21. Institutional investors led the demand, with their portion subscribed 12.68 times, while the retail portion was subscribed 1.39 times. The IPO was entirely an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 126.4 million shares by 10 existing shareholders, including state-owned insurers and banks.

The NSE did not issue any fresh shares and will therefore receive no proceeds from the offering. After issue-related expenses, the proceeds will go to the selling shareholders. The exchange had first approached the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) to go public nearly a decade ago, but its listing plans were held up by regulatory proceedings related to its past co-location and dark fibre arrangements.

In July, Sebi agreed to settlement terms of 1,491 crore for the co-location and dark fibre cases, clearing a key regulatory hurdle for the listing. The NSE had earlier planned an issue of about 30,000 crore, which would have made it India's largest IPO, surpassing Hyundai Motor India's 27,870-crore offering in October 2024.

The exchange subsequently reduced the issue size to about 22,500 crore. The Life Insurance Corporation of India is the biggest shareholder, with its holding valued at around 48,620 crore. It is followed by Aranda Investments Mauritius and Stock Holding Corporation, with holdings valued at a little over 20,000 crore each.

SBI Capital's holding is valued at around 19,650 crore, while State Bank of India owns shares worth around 14,634 crore. The value of the holdings is based on NSE's Thursday closing price of 1,818 on the BSE. Among other prominent shareholders are D-Mart owner Radhakishan Damani, whose holding is valued at around 7,164 crore, and Hero MotoCorp's Sunil Kant Munjal, whose stake is worth around 1,870 crore.

Wipro founder Azim Premji's PI Opportunities holds shares valued at around 10,667 crore, while Infosys co-founder N R Narayana Murthy's Catamaran Ventures owns shares worth around 705 crore. S Gopalakrishnan, a former Infosys senior executive, Hexaware Technologies founder Atul Nishar, Avenue Supermarts' former MD and CEO Ignatius Navil Noronha, Haldiram Snacks MD Manohar Lal Agarwal, Sobha chairman PNC Menon and Samco Group chairman Vipul Jayantilal Modi are among the other long-standing shareholders with sizeable holdings in NSE.

title: NSE Debuts at 1,800, Ends Day as 11th Largest Indian Co by Value
